translationRepairs: He was the youngest son of Wei Gongxuan, Duke of Wei, who had served as chief councilor under Emperor Xuanzong.
He was the youngest son of Cui Xuan, Duke of Wei, who had served as chief councilor in the Dazhong era.

Focus unit 大中時宰相魏公鉉之幼子也 titles the father as 魏公 plus given name 鉉, not a fused Wei Gongxuan; surrounding 崔沂 supplies the surname Cui. Timing is the era name 大中時, not an invented Emperor Xuanzong. The proposed wording matches that parsing.
The minister concurred and moved him to the post of grand censor.
The minister concurred and moved him to the post of Grand Master of Remonstrance.

Focus unit moves him 移為諫議大夫; that office is Grand Master of Remonstrance, not a censorate post (御史). The later 御史司憲 posting in s0030 confirms the distinction. The proposed title corrects the mistranslation.
According to the New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers, the Feng clan had long resided in Raoyang County in Bohai.
According to the New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers, the Feng clan had long resided in Tiao County in Bohai.
Focus unit places the Feng clan in 渤海蓚縣; 蓚縣 is Tiao County, not Raoyang (饒陽). The proposed place name restores the Chinese toponym.
